summary: Robert Duquenne (1944–2013) worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He held a post as a Tantric Buddhism specialist at Hōbōgirin (attested 1981) and was affiliated with the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2009).

Robert E. Buswell Jr. is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his A.B., M.A., and Ph.D. at UC Berkeley. He joined UCLA around 1986, serving as department chair, Center for Buddhist Studies director, and later Distinguished Professor Emeritus.

Robert E. Harrist, Jr. is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Columbia University, where he is attested as the Jane and Leopold Swergold Professor Emeritus of Chinese Art History in 2026.

Robert E. Morrell specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies, studying under Robert H. Brower and William H. McCullough. He held posts at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 1985 and 2006).

Robert E. Svoboda is an Indologist who studied at the University of Oklahoma and under Aghori Vimalananda. In 2008, he was an adjunct member at The Ayurvedic Institute, Bastyr University, and the Institute for Religion and Health.
Robert E. W. Iggleden (1913–1981) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sayadaw U Thittila until 1952. He served as Secretary of the Pali Text Society until 1976.

Robert Ernest Hume (1877–1948) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Yale, Union Theological Seminary, and the University of Göttingen, and served as Professor of History of Religions at Union Theological Seminary (1914–1943).
Robert F. Rhodes works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He was a Ph.D. candidate at Harvard University and served as a professor at Otani University, attested between 1993 and 2014.
Robert Fazy (1872–1956) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Tibetology. He earned his Dr.jur. at the University of Geneva by 1899 and founded the Swiss Asia Society in 1939.

Robert Florida specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University, and was later an Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria (attested 2000–2005).

Robert Ford Campany is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He taught as a professor at Indiana University Bloomington (~1989–2006), held a post at USC (~2006–2010), and became Professor at Vanderbilt University in 2010.

Robert Gardner (1925–2014) earned his B.A. at Harvard University, where he later served as a professor (1956–1997) and founded a unit in 1957. He also held positions at Harvard Art Museums and the University of Puget Sound.

Robert Gauthiot (1876–1916) specialized in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at EPHE and earned a PhD at the University of Paris under Antoine Meillet, later becoming directeur d’études adjoint at EPHE in 1905.

Robert Gordon Latham (1812–1888) studied at Cambridge and under Rasmus Rask. A linguist and physician, he was Professor of English Language at UCL (1839) and directed the ethnological department at The Crystal Palace (~1852–1863).

Robert Göbl (1919–1997) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and archaeology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (1948–1950), where he later served as PD (1955) and Director (1965–1989).

Robert H. Brower (1923–1988) was a Japanologist educated at Harvard and Michigan. He taught at Minnesota and Stanford, directed the Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies, and chaired Far Eastern Languages and Literatures at Michigan (1966–1988).

Robert H. Sharf studied at Toronto, Kyoto, and Michigan. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, he taught at McMaster and Michigan before becoming D. H. Chen Distinguished Professor of Buddhist Studies at UC Berkeley around 2003.

Robert Hamilton Blair Williams (1915–1975) was an Indologist who completed his B.A. and Ph.D. at SOAS under Ralph Lilley Turner. He worked at the India Office Records (1939–1946) and lectured in Indo-Aryan and Jaina Studies at SOAS (1949–1953).

Robert Henry Lawson Slater (1896–1984) studied at Cambridge and Columbia. He taught at Rangoon, Union Theological Seminary, and McGill, served as Dean of Theology at Huron University College, and was Professor of World Religions at Harvard (1958–1964).
Robert Hinde (1923–2016) was educated at St John's College and Balliol College, Oxford (~1947–1950). He held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1950 to 1994.
